questions.question: A budget differs from a financial statement in that:
options: A budget ESTIMATES the planned future while a statement REPORTS the provable past — and every variance between them must be explained
A budget is always more accurate
A statement is drawn before the events
Budgets are optional records of the past

questions.question: The question the cash budget answers is:
options: What was last year's profit?
The survival question — can we pay our way each month?
What mark-up should be charged?
Which debtors should be written off?

questions.question: The capital budget is the plan for:
options: Daily grocery spending
The owner's drawings
Buying long-life assets — machinery, vehicles, equipment — planned apart from daily running
Monthly wage payments

questions.question: Zero-based budgeting demands that:
options: Every line is last year's figure plus a percentage
The budget must total zero
Only brand-new costs are questioned
Every line begins at NOTHING and argues for its whole amount afresh — so dead costs die instead of riding along

questions.question: October's receipts of R30 000 for Lerato's Woodcraft comprise:
options: Cash sales of R21 000 plus the collection of September's credit sales of R9 000 (30% of R30 000)
October's full sales, cash and credit together
Cash sales only
September's total sales

questions.question: A credit sale enters the cash budget:
options: In the month the invoice is issued
When the money ARRIVES — a month later, at collection; the cash budget thinks in cash alone
Half now, half later
Never — credit sales are left out entirely

questions.question: November's closing balance is:
options: R4 000 — opening R8 000 plus routine surplus R5 000 minus the lathe's R9 000
Negative R4 000

questions.question: The cash budget's fixed skeleton runs:
options: Closing, opening, payments, receipts
Payments first, then receipts, then closing
In whatever order the month suggests
Receipts; payments; surplus or deficit; opening balance; closing balance — each closing rolling into the next opening

subtopics.title: Reading the Budget — the Decisions Inside

questions.question: The budget's "first gift" shown by the lathe purchase is:
options: TIMING — big purchases are placed where the balances can hold them, seen in advance
A discount on the machine
Avoiding capital purchases altogether
Hiding the payment from the bank

questions.question: If the projected balance had dipped below zero, the cheap-while-early options are:
options: Hope the sales improve
Shift the lathe a month later, or arrange an overdraft IN ADVANCE — banks price planned requests kindly and desperate ones dearly
Skip the wages that month
Stop paying the rent

questions.question: Because of the credit-sales lag, when sales GROW:
options: Cash arrives sooner than before
The lag disappears
A bumper month's cash lands only AFTER that month's costs were paid — growth can feel tight in cash
Nothing changes in the cash budget

questions.question: "A budgeted business meets its troubles as variances" means:
options: A budget prevents all trouble
Variances must be punished
Problems stop being visible
Actual figures line up beside estimates, and every gap becomes an investigation months before it becomes an emergency

subtopics.title: The Wider Family and the Year's Close

questions.question: The capital budget serves the cash budget by:
options: Supplying the landing dates and amounts of planned asset purchases — assets arriving by plan, not appetite
Replacing it completely
Keeping large purchases out of the books
Recording monthly depreciation

questions.question: Medium-term and long-term budgets differ in that:
options: Only one of them uses rands
Medium-term plans one to three years out (range, staffing); long-term carries the strategy further, in broader strokes
Long-term budgets are the more precise ones
Medium-term budgets ignore money entirely

questions.question: Depreciation never appears in a cash budget because:
options: The amount is too small to matter
It belongs in the capital budget instead
No rand LEAVES — the cash budget records only actual money movements
It is recorded weekly, not monthly

questions.question: The commenting habits for budget questions are:
options: Restate the totals in words
Praise every figure given
Convert every figure to a percentage
A dip is a timing question; a shortfall is a financing question; a variance is an investigation question

subtopics.title: The Month Written Before It Happens

questions.question: "A report is a rear-view mirror; a budget is the headlights" means:
options: Statements look backward at proved events; the budget looks forward so the month can be steered instead of endured
Reports are easier to read
Budgets make statements unnecessary
Mirrors are more reliable than headlights

questions.question: The household page listing the pay coming in and the rent, groceries and transport going out IS:
options: A statement of financial position
A cash budget — the same tool as the workshop's and the city's, differing only in zeros
An income statement
A fixed asset register

questions.question: Writing the plan down matters because:
options: Written plans spend less by themselves
The bank requires it
A plan that was never written can never be CHECKED — the page turns 'the money just disappeared' into precise, answerable questions
It replaces the source documents

subtopics.title: Watching the Purse Through Three Months

questions.question: The quarter's purse runs:
options: Opens R3 000; October closes R8 000; November dips to R4 000; December recovers to R9 000
Opens R3 000 and closes R3 000
Opens R8 000; closes R4 000 in December
Negative in every month

questions.question: November was safe for Lerato but dangerous for the neighbour because:
options: The neighbour paid more for the lathe
Lerato SAW the dip on paper in advance and confirmed the purse could take it; the neighbour bought on a good feeling in a lean month
The neighbour had no wages to pay
Lathes cost less in December

questions.question: "Earning and receiving keep different calendars" refers to:
options: Weekends and public holidays
The financial year end
The credit-sales lag — 30% of each month's sales arrives a month late, so a strong month can still feel squeezed
The difference between wages and salaries

subtopics.title: Why Every Rand Must Re-Apply for Its Job

questions.question: "Dead costs love a copied list" means:
options: Copied budgets carry forgotten, useless lines forever — the unwatched streaming service, the outdated arrangement
Photocopies fade over time
Old budgets must be shredded
Costs double when written twice

questions.question: Zero-based budgeting "dismisses the entire list" by asking of each line:
options: Who approved this last year?
Why does this line exist, what does it buy us NOW, and what actually breaks if we cut it?
Which lines are the largest?
Which lines are the oldest?

questions.question: The trade-off of zero-based budgeting is:
options: It cannot be used by households
It needs no records at all
Harder work than copying — repaid in recovered rands whenever it is done honestly
It doubles every budget line

questions.question: The year's complete toolkit ends with:
options: Only journals and ledgers
Statements without any analysis
Marketing and selling skills
Recording, posting, reconciling, adjusting, closing, reporting, analysing, costing — and budgeting: stewardship from corner shop to city
